content.title: Forecasters eye possible ‘super El Niño’ in 2026
content.text: NOAA boosts El Niño forecast confidence to 60% The Climate Prediction Center and other agencies now place El Niño odds at around 58–61% by mid-to-late 2026, up from earlier in the year. This shift follows weakening La Niña conditions and the emergence of subsurface Pacific warmth, both precursors to El Niño. While neutral conditions are expected through summer, model consensus increasingly tilts toward warming in the Niño 3.4 region later in the year. Morning Overview + 1 What a 'super El Niño' could mean for the world European and NOAA models suggest the possibility of a 'super El Niño,' where Pacific warming exceeds 2°C, potentially ranking among the strongest on record. Such an event could suppress Atlantic hurricanes, intensify heatwaves, shift rainfall patterns across continents, and make 2027 a contender for the hottest year ever. Past strong El Niños have triggered widespread drought in Australia and India, storms in the Pacific, and global coral bleaching. Newser + 1 Scientists urge caution amid forecast uncertainty Despite converging signs, forecasters emphasize the 'spring predictability barrier,' when model skill is historically low. Current atmospheric patterns still reflect weak La Niña influence, and key triggers like slackening trade winds have yet to occur consistently. Experts stress that while probabilities are rising, a full El Niño is not guaranteed, and intensity remains uncertain until closer to summer. Morning Overview + 1 From La Niña to neutral: The road to El Niño The transition from a weak La Niña to ENSO-neutral is underway, with neutral conditions expected to dominate through spring and early summer. This phase allows other climate drivers—such as Atlantic and Indian Ocean temperatures—to shape seasonal weather in the U.S. and globally. The last El Niño in 2023–2024 set heat records and fueled costly disasters, heightening concern over what a new cycle could bring. Morning Overview + 1 Next forecast milestones to watch The next ENSO Diagnostic Discussion on March 12, 2026, will reassess Pacific conditions and update probabilities for El Niño, La Niña, or continued neutrality. By early summer, forecasters expect improved confidence as the predictability barrier lessens, allowing clearer assessment of whether subsurface warmth will translate into a full El Niño. Climate Impact Company also projects the potential for El Niño in 2026 followed by La Niña in 2027, which would bring contrasting climate influences over consecutive years.
